accuracy.evidence: Checked against the GB Non-native Species Secretariat and the Mammal Society: grey squirrels were introduced from North America from the 1870s (first recorded release 1876), they digest acorns while still green (high tannin) which reds cannot, and they carry squirrelpox virus with few symptoms while it is usually fatal to reds; Mammal Society 2018 estimates are about 2.7 million greys and about 287,000 reds, so 'millions of greys and few reds' is right. Australian Museum and the Australian Government environment department: about 100 (101–102) cane toads from Hawaii (originally South/Central America) were brought to Queensland in 1935 to control cane beetles; the beetles live high on cane stalks and the toads did not control them; bufotoxin from the parotoid glands kills quolls, goannas and snakes that eat them. 24 wild rabbits were released by Thomas Austin near Geelong in 1859 and spread to hundreds of millions. Anglesey red squirrel recovery after grey removal is documented by Red Squirrels Trust Wales. Squirrel and rabbit numbers are labelled as simple models in the adult text and banner. Parameterised answers (9n, r−k, 8n, r+g) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented ideas in teacher guidance from the Royal Society of Biology and NNSS education packs: 'invasive means big or dangerous' (challenge tag scary), 'every non-native species is harmful' and its opposite (tags allbad and neverbad, mastery m5), 'greys kill reds by fighting' (tag fight, mastery m8), 'reds just moved away' (tag moved), 'cane toads did their job on the beetles' (step 2 predict, tag beetles), 'bring a predator from abroad to fix it' (decoy action in step 5 and mastery m2), and 'native means native everywhere' (mastery m9). Each wrong answer has its own message.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (well under 30% against every flagship lab). The nearest topics are 627 Reading food web diagrams (flagfoodweb removes species from a web), 874 Predator hunting strategies (flaghunt) and 909 Matter cycling (flagmatcyc). None models a newcomer species: this lab runs red and grey squirrel populations year by year, drags a cane toad between its intended target and native predators, and compares fields with and without hunters. It could not be relabelled for another topic.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is discovered before it is named: tapping the wood year by year shows reds falling as greys rise while the year messages give the two causes (green acorns, squirrelpox); dragging the toad to the cane shows it cannot reach the beetles and to native predators shows poisoning; running both rabbit fields shows 30 rabbits with hunters against 5,832 without and the grass turning bare; only then does the sort step name the four kinds of harm, and the last step turns that into prevention.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'room for both' and 'greys die out because the wood is new' for the squirrels, 'ate the beetles and saved the crop' for the cane toads (the original plan), and '24, the same as before' or 'a few hundred' for the rabbits. The lab then disproves each one and the task message names the prediction and the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its own feedback: scary, native, fight, moved, beetles, slow, fed, report, protect, allbad, neverbad. For example choosing 'Greys fight and kill the reds' explains they win by eating the food first and carrying squirrelpox; choosing 'They ate all the cane beetles' explains the beetles live high up the cane out of reach. Correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores Flesch-Kincaid 5.0 (limit 6.5) and adult text 6.6 (limit 9.5). Sentences are short; native, invasive species, squirrelpox, predator and poison are each explained in plain words where they first appear, and lab buttons use plain verbs ('Next year', 'Move the toad to: Quoll', 'Put it in: Spreads disease').

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation shares under 12% of 6-word shingles with every other lesson. Each kid paragraph carries one case or idea (definition, grey squirrels, cane toads, rabbits and prevention); the adult text gives standards, sources, the task list with the model caveat, and common mistakes.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark themes, before and after Show me at every step (/workspace/shots/inv-*, invd-*). After a first pass the squirrel legend was moved above the bars (it covered the year 7–8 grey bars), the rabbit field titles were shortened to 'With hunters' and 'No hunters' (they overlapped at 360 px) and the challenge chart no longer shows the tap hint. Cards, bins and action buttons now fit without clipping, and every action also has a full-width button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes and there are no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Next year, Move the toad to, Pick then Put it in, action cards), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the state (year and both squirrel counts, places tried, rabbits in each field, cards sorted), and feedback is announced through c.say.
